criteria.extend_existing_packages: Place the owner-scoped calls as new members of the current process, files and codec packages, adding no package. Existing identities and registration stay untouched while owner-mediated members share packages with direct Bun members; the allowlist is the set of added members.
criteria.single_test_package: Create exactly one fresh package, can.std.test@1, covering all base owner, workspace, process and evidence calls behind opaque constructorless handles. One catalogue member per permitted native call makes the listing itself the dispatch allowlist, leaving open-ended dispatch/eval inexpressible. A single emitter contribution points the identities at $canTest entry points supplied by owner.ts and transport.ts. Unknown handles die at lookup; retired handles die at liveness.
criteria.split_owner_test_packages: Create can.std.owner@1 for grant identity with transport primitives and can.std.test@1 for workspace, process and evidence calls. Identity/transport and domain calls live in distinct reserved packages with distinct factories and emitter contributions.

binding_shape.instructions: Select the packaging and dispatch arrangement that meets every acceptance clause with the smallest closed mechanism.

state: Repository github.com/veighnsche/can-lang, a Can language compiler. The file compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json is the single hand-edited source listing 306 operations in 38 packages at revision 1 for target bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1. The cataloguegen tool derives Go constants, the frozen TypeScript mirror, the reserved error registry and standard-library docs from it, and its check mode reports drift without edits. A fresh package enters as can.std.<name>@<revision>, turns reserved on load, and collides loudly on any repeated identity. Handles that must never be forged are represented as opaque types without constructors (precedent: can.prelude@1::standard_failure exposing projections). During emission every domain contributes a bindingContribution table from operation identity to runtime target; combineBindingContributions joins them in a fixed sequence and refuses duplicates (precedent: can.std.process@1::run becomes $canProcesses.run, created by createProcesses within shared state; Bun-only state hides behind !browser tests). Runtime helpers are factories over $canDomain and numeric error ids, checked by adjacent bun:test files under oxlint, oxfmt and tsc. Fixed wire shapes: P02 envelopes carry schema_version "1", a 1..256 byte owner_grant, a 1..128 character operation, a sha256 arguments digest, a deadline clock of n-monotonic or wall-utc, outcome/kind words where completed demands ok, and no more than 32 facts/partial members; P10 confirms spawn-start owners through table lookup; K17 fixes launch descriptors 0-4; the lifecycle bans omitted-means-unlimited limits. P28 needs to introduce the first owner, workspace, process and evidence bindings by editing catalogue.json and cataloguegen, creating runtime/test-support/transport.ts with owner.ts, and creating compiler/internal/emit/test_operations.go. It passes when catalogue, checker and emitter concur on effects and opaque admission, when forged or stale owners, open-ended dispatch/eval, unboxed thenables and mistaken targets all fail, when mirrors regenerate byte-identically, and the whole delta remains provisional until P26.
